$comment: Single source registry. The README attribution section, the confidence badges, the cache TTLs and the CORS probe all read from this file. licenseClass drives the adapter isolation required by decision 3: any source with licenseClass 'nc' or 'share-alike' must be reached through its own adapter module and its data must never be merged into a general-purpose derived table.

licenseClasses.open: Public domain, CC0, CC BY, or equivalent. Free to use, redistribute and merge.
licenseClasses.nc: Non-commercial only. Usable by this project (non-commercial, no ads, no paid tier) but must be isolated behind its own adapter so a change in project status means swapping one module.
licenseClasses.share-alike: Copyleft (ODbL, CC BY-SA). Derived datasets inherit the licence. Must be stored separately and never merged into a general-purpose derived table.
licenseClasses.restricted: No licence grant for reuse. Not ingested. Link-out only.
licenseClasses.restricted-minimal: No general licence grant, but minimal attributed elements are ingested: facts and figures rendered with source credit and a link back (a headline, outlet, timestamp and link; or a numeric value with its source named). Never bulk redistribution, never the full work. Everything else is link-out. Enforced by scripts/licence-posture.mjs, not by convention.
licenseClasses.share-alike-nc: Non-commercial AND copyleft (CC BY-NC-SA). Both obligations bind: usable by this project because it is non-commercial (decision 3), and derived datasets inherit the licence so they are stored separately and never merged into a general-purpose derived table. Neither term may be dropped because the other is recorded.

sources.attribution: Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP), Georeferenced Event Dataset v26.1 (CC BY 4.0), with the dataset publications cited as the licence requires.
sources.notes: Bulk CSV download, not the REST API. The API at ucdpapi.pcr.uu.se now answers 401 on EVERY endpoint and version tested (gedevents 24.1 and 26.1, ucdpprioconflict, battledeaths, nonstate, onesided): "API token required. Add header: x-ucdp-access-token". The bulk downloads at ucdp.uu.se/downloads are keyless and still CC BY 4.0 — verified 200, application/x-zip-compressed, 39.1MB, PK zip magic. An annually-released dataset does not need a live API, so the keyless path is preferred and no key is introduced. ARCHITECTURE CONSEQUENCE, undecided: at 39MB this is not a per-visitor browser fetch. It wants version-pinning as a bundled dataset (which under A6a requires a registered byte-level shape assertion) or a Worker-side extract. Not a runtime client fetch either way. Annual release, NOT a live feed; the layer header must state version and coverage end date.

sources.name: IMF PortWatch — daily chokepoint transit data
sources.license: IMF — all rights reserved. No reuse grant identified.
sources.notes: LICENCE READING, 2026-08-14 — the terms could not be read from this machine and were NOT accepted. The dataset item states "© 2022 INTERNATIONAL MONETARY FUND. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED" with no reuse grant. The licence URL in PortWatch own metadata (imf.org/external/terms.htm) is DEAD — it redirects into a 404 handler — and the live terms page (imf.org/en/About/copyright-and-terms) returns 403 from Akamai. Both are walls, not evidence: no answer about the terms is not an answer that they are permissive (rule 30). Treated like the RSS feeds — render figures with attribution and link out, never redistribute the dataset. UNITS (rule 22) — capacity* are trade volumes in METRIC TONS. The authority for that is the catalogue item description, NOT the service field metadata, which carries empty descriptions and aliases that merely echo field names. The contract test asserts the two do not disagree rather than silently preferring either. TIER SPLIT — n_* are COUNTED transit calls (OFFICIAL). capacity* are payload ESTIMATES the IMF itself describes as modelled from vessel length, width, draft, capacity and block coefficient times deadweight tonnage (Arslanalp, Koepke & Verschuur, IMF WP/2021/225). Rendering capacity as OFFICIAL would assert a measured tonnage the source calls an estimate. CAVEATS — whether the IMF documents the GPS-jamming / AIS-spoofing / dark-vessel limitations could not be established: the site is a JS-rendered ArcGIS Hub app that did not hydrate under the checking browser, so the result is inconclusive, not negative. The panel caveat therefore renders as OUR statement about AIS-derived data with its basis cited, never as theirs.

sources.name: WHO Disease Outbreak News
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO — WHO publications are open access under this licence (who.int/about/policies/publishing/copyright, read 2026-08-14).
sources.attribution: Disease Outbreak News, World Health Organization (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO).
sources.notes: LICENCE READ 2026-08-14 — CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO. Non-commercial suits decision 3; attribution is mandatory; share-alike binds derivative works. Classified share-alike rather than nc because the share-alike constraint is the one that shapes code (derived tables must stay separate), while non-commercial is satisfied by the project standing. NO REGISTRY CLASS EXPRESSES BOTH — see OPEN-QUESTIONS 9. WHAT IS INGESTED — headline, publication date and a link back, requested via  so WHO full text (Overview, Epidemiology, Assessment, Advice) never crosses the network. Headlines are WHO wording, never rewritten. NO COUNTRY IS PARSED FROM A TITLE. The payload carries no structured country field and titles include "Multi-locations" entries, so attaching a country would assert a link WHO did not publish. See src/sources/who-don.ts. ORDERING IS EXPLICIT — the unordered default returned a page whose newest entry was 18 months stale while the true newest was published that morning.

sources.name: UNHCR Refugee Data Finder — population statistics
sources.license: Not established from this machine. SPEC-EXPANSION asserts CC BY 4.0; that assertion is UNVERIFIED here.
sources.notes: LICENCE READING ATTEMPTED 2026-08-14 AND FAILED — recorded per L15 as a conservative class, not a verified one. unhcr.org/refugee-statistics/insights/explainers/terms-of-use.html and unhcr.org/terms-and-conditions both return 403 from this network. The API docs at api.unhcr.org/docs/refugee-statistics.html were fetched and searched in full (293KB of text): they contain no CC BY, no Creative Commons, no copyright statement — only the Apache licence of the OpenAPI generator that built the page, which is the tooling and not the data. SPEC-EXPANSION Phase A3 asserts CC BY 4.0; a spec claim is not a reading. Classified restricted-minimal deliberately: it permits exactly what this app does (figures with attribution and a link back) and over-claims nothing. UPGRADE TO open IF CC BY 4.0 IS VERIFIED — under-claiming rights is recoverable, over-claiming is the violation. See OPEN-QUESTIONS 10. THREE-STATE ENCODING — a single row mixes types and the types carry meaning: a number is a reported figure, the STRING "0" is a reported zero, and the STRING "-" is no data. Number("-") is NaN, so Number(v) || 0 would render no-data as a counted zero. Measured on the 2023 asylum breakdown: 662 numbers, 778 reported zeros, 162 dashes. A country with NO ROW (73 ISO3 codes) is a fourth state and renders as no data, never as zeros. BREAKDOWN IS MANDATORY — without coa_all/coo_all the API returns one world-aggregate row whose codes are both "-", which reads like a per-country response until inspected. The adapter drops that row rather than filing a global total under a country.

sources.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue (cisagov mirror)
sources.license: CC0 1.0 Universal — public domain dedication. Read 2026-08-14 from the mirror LICENSE file and README.
sources.notes: LICENCE READ 2026-08-14 AND VERIFIED — CC0 1.0 Universal. The mirror LICENSE file states "The KEV database is distributed under the Creative Commons 0 1.0 License. You may use this data in any legal manner", and the README confirms it matches cisa.gov/sites/default/files/licenses/kev/license.txt. One restriction that is NOT a data restriction: use of the data does not authorise use of the CISA Logo or DHS Seal, and must not be read as endorsement. This app renders neither. NOTE GitHub reports the repo licence as NOASSERTION because its detector does not recognise the prefixed text; the file itself is the full CC0 legal code. MIRROR ONLY, NEVER cisa.gov — direct fetches have been rate-limited and IP-blocked. Asserted by contract test. develop is the repository default branch; a pinned commit would be reproducible and permanently stale, which is the wrong trade for a catalogue whose value is being current. THREE-STATE FIELD — knownRansomwareCampaignUse is "Known" or "Unknown", and Unknown means CISA has NO EVIDENCE either way, not that the vulnerability is unused by ransomware. 1316 of 1665 entries are Unknown, so a boolean coercion would assert something CISA never said about the majority of the catalogue. Modelled as a three-state with the caveat attached to the fact. NO COUNTRY DIMENSION — KEV lists vulnerabilities, not jurisdictions or victims. Nothing is attributed to a country.

sources.name: Ember — yearly electricity generation
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 — read 2026-08-14 at ember-energy.org/creative-commons/: "Ember content is released under a Creative Commons Attribution Licence (CC-BY-4.0)". Logo use requires separate permission and is not used.
sources.notes: BLOCKED ON A KEY — the API returns 403 {"detail":"No API key set"}. The key is free but requires a signup that cannot be completed autonomously, so NO LIVE RESPONSE HAS BEEN CAPTURED and verifiedAgainst stays "documentation", which blocks deployment by design (A6). See OPEN-QUESTIONS 11. LICENCE READ AND VERIFIED 2026-08-14 at ember-energy.org/creative-commons/ — CC BY 4.0, share and adapt with credit. This is a genuine reading, not a spec claim, and not rule-derived. Ember logo use needs separate permission; not used. A KEYLESS PATH EXISTS AND IS NOT USABLE AS-IS — files.ember-energy.org publishes release_generation_yearly_global.csv (16.0MB) and release_generation_yearly_lower.csv (4.1MB) without a key, but NEITHER SENDS access-control-allow-origin, so a browser cannot read them: they are worker-required, and the Worker does not exist. Their size also rules them out as fixtures. Recorded in FOUND.md rather than worked around. SHAPE NOTES for whoever lands this: the CSV mixes country rows with regional aggregates (Area type = Region, blank ISO 3 code) and carries an "Is aggregated source" flag, so summing rows naively double-counts. It also distinguishes a reported 0.0 from an empty cell -- the same rule 30 distinction UNHCR needed.

verifiedAgainstValues.documentation: Endpoint contract taken from vendor documentation. NOT confirmed against a live response. Blocks deployment.
verifiedAgainstValues.live: Confirmed against a live response captured by npm run probe, with the observed shape recorded in a fixture.
verifiedAgainstValues.bundled: Not fetched at runtime. Shipped from a version-pinned package and asserted byte-level against the real data by the test suite. Passes the gate, and is listed by name in every gate run rather than being skipped.
